segments.en: Maglev trains, a fusion of “magnetic” and “levitation,” utilize magnetism to offer a fast and smooth railway service.
segments.zh: 磁浮列車（maglev）這個字是「磁力」和「懸浮」的結合，它利用磁力提供快速又平穩的鐵路服務。

segments.en: Instead of wheels, these trains have special electromagnetic systems 41 them up and move them forward.
segments.zh: 這種列車沒有輪子，而是有特殊的電磁系統（41）它們往上推，並帶動它們前進。

segments.en: They zoom along the tracks at incredible speeds, far exceeding those of traditional trains.
segments.zh: 它們以驚人的速度沿著軌道飛馳，遠遠超過傳統列車。

segments.en: They can achieve speeds above 300 miles per hour, 42 bullet trains usually go around 200 miles per hour.
segments.zh: 它們的時速可以超過 300 英里，（42）子彈列車通常大約是時速 200 英里。

segments.en: What makes maglev trains special is that they don’t touch the ground, so there is no friction, which means they can go extremely fast without any 43 .
segments.zh: 磁浮列車特別的地方在於不接觸地面，所以沒有摩擦力，也就是說可以在沒有任何（43）的情況下跑得非常快。

segments.en: Right now, there are only a limited number of these amazing trains in 44 , but they are expected to become more popular in the future.
segments.zh: 目前只有少數這種驚人的列車在（44）中，但預期將來會更普及。

segments.en: They operate quietly, are cost-effective to maintain, and produce minimal pollution 45 to certain other types of trains.
segments.zh: 它們運行安靜、維護成本划算，而且和某些其他類型的列車（45），產生的污染極少。

segments.en: In fact, it is predicted that they may be even as popular as air transportation one day!
segments.zh: 事實上，有人預測它們有一天可能和航空運輸一樣普及！

segments.en: We all have the same number of hours each day, and it’s up to us to decide how we spend them.
segments.zh: 我們每個人每天都有同樣多的時間，怎麼用由我們自己決定。

segments.en: According to “the 5-hour rule,” how we choose to spend those hours might mean the difference between success and mediocrity.
segments.zh: 依照「五小時法則」，我們選擇怎麼用這些時間，可能就是成功與平庸的差別。

segments.en: There are 24 hours in a day.
segments.zh: 一天有 24 小時。

segments.en: The average person sleeps around eight hours, with the Dutch sleeping the most and the Singaporeans the least.
segments.zh: 一般人大約睡八小時，其中荷蘭人睡最多，新加坡人睡最少。

segments.en: After we subtract 7 hours of working time, we’re down to 9 remaining hours.
segments.zh: 扣掉 7 小時的工作時間後，只剩 9 小時。

segments.en: Much of those 9 hours are taken up by shopping, housework, unpaid labor (e.g. care work), eating and drinking.
segments.zh: 這 9 小時裡，有很多被購物、家事、無酬勞動（例如照顧工作）、吃喝占掉。

segments.en: Of course, there are massive cultural differences.
segments.zh: 當然，文化差異非常大。

segments.en: For instance, people in France, Greece, Italy and Spain report spending more time eating than people in most other European countries.
segments.zh: 例如，法國、希臘、義大利和西班牙的人表示，他們花在吃飯的時間比大多數其他歐洲國家的人多。

segments.en: The country where people spend the least time eating and drinking is the USA (63 minutes).
segments.zh: 花最少時間吃喝的國家是美國（63 分鐘）。

segments.en: Most people have at least a few hours to do with what they want.
segments.zh: 大多數人至少有幾個小時可以做自己想做的事。

segments.en: For more than half of the population, those hours are wasted away on non-work-related phone worship.
segments.zh: 對超過一半的人來說，這些時間都浪費在和工作無關的滑手機上。

segments.en: But these are not the people who will become the entrepreneurs, innovators, and success stories of tomorrow.
segments.zh: 但這些人不會成為明日的創業家、創新者和成功故事的主角。

segments.en: The “5-hour rule” is the rule where we spend one hour a day learning, reflecting, and thinking.
segments.zh: 「五小時法則」是每天花一小時學習、反思和思考。

segments.en: We do this five times a week, which makes up the “5-hour” rule.
segments.zh: 一星期做五次，合起來就是「五小時」法則。

segments.en: The rule dates to Benjamin Franklin, who would devote an hour each day specifically to learning something new.
segments.zh: 這個法則可以追溯到班傑明．富蘭克林，他每天會特別撥出一小時學新東西。

segments.en: Today, Elon Musk, Oprah Winfrey, and Bill Gates all employ some version of the 5-hour rule.
segments.zh: 現在，伊隆．馬斯克、歐普拉．溫芙蕾和比爾．蓋茲都採用某種版本的五小時法則。

segments.en: So, why not give the 5-hour rule a go?
segments.zh: 所以，何不試試五小時法則？

segments.en: At worst, it will make you a bit more interesting at the next family gathering.
segments.zh: 最差的情況，它會讓你在下次家庭聚會上變得有趣一點。

segments.en: At best, it might make you a few million dollars.
segments.zh: 最好的情況，它可能讓你賺進幾百萬美元。
